title: An Autonomous, Preregistered Evaluation of a Deterministic Provenance‑Scoring Judge for LLM NetOps "No‑Issue" Assertions
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired confirmatory evaluation of a deterministic provenance+validator judge designed to reduce unsupported LLM "no‑issue" (reachability / health‑holds) assertions in scripted NetOps emulator scenarios. Using gpt-5-mini and the frozen preregistration cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1, the autonomous run produced 166 completed episodes (14 failed after preregistered retries) yielding 83 complete paired tasks. Baseline (LLM only) success = 81/83 (97.59%); guarded (judge) success = 83/83 (100.0%). Absolute paired improvement = 0.0240963855; paired bootstrap 95% CI (percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.50. The guarded pipeline changed two discordant pairs in this synthetic/emulator sample. The observed change is numerically small and statistically inconclusive at the realized paired sample size. All execution artifacts and per‑file SHA256 digests are preserved in the run manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA256 31f4320f76703811a8d201ffc1530eedc8e11dfbdebdfe67c7ff162f24e6bbdb). Conclusions are strictly bounded to the preregistered synthetic/emulator domain; production claims are not supported by this run.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in NetOps/AIOps for diagnosis, intent translation, and limited remediation. A recurring operational failure mode is a fluent but unsupported "no‑issue" assertion (e.g., "reachability holds"), which can mislead operators or automated workflows. We asked: can a deterministic, programmatic provenance+validator judge—combining retrieval grounding, protocol‑aware syntactic/semantic validators, and telemetry cross‑checks—reduce unsupported LLM "no‑issue" assertions when ground truth is available programmatically? We preregistered a paired experimental design (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1), executed the study autonomously using gpt-5-mini, and recorded full execution provenance. Our contribution is an evidence‑grounded, fully auditable, preregistered autonomous evaluation and a bounded empirical assessment in scripted NetOps emulator scenarios.
sections.related_work: Operational reliability for LLMs depends on layered controls (generate→validate→repair) and evidence grounding; recent surveys and engineering studies emphasize layered grounding, verifier‑assisted pipelines, and workflow‑centered evaluation for agentic NetOps/AIOps. Prior work motivates combining retrieval grounding, structured validators, and telemetry checks to reduce hallucination-like unsupported assertions. We cite representative, verified sources that informed our design and judge components.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1 froze the paired design (90 seeded emulator tasks), random seeds, retry/replacement rules (≤2 retries), maximum_model_calls=180, primary/secondary estimands, and a detailed analysis plan. Task/adapter: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Judge pipeline (frozen): (A) deterministic retrieval grounding against a preregistered snapshot index, (B) protocol‑aware syntactic/semantic validators for canonical NetOps properties (reachability/forwarding, interface admin/down), (C) deterministic telemetry cross‑checks consuming emulator state. Execution: for each seeded scenario a shared_initial generation produced a candidate assertion; two paired episodes were produced per task (baseline: LLM-only; guarded: judge applied). Parser and scoring: a deterministic parser extracted the canonical single "no‑issue/reachability holds" assertion per episode (extra assertions appended to audit logs per preregistration). Missingness/retries: preregistered deterministic policies governed retries and deterministic replacements to preserve task_count. Analysis (frozen): primary confirmatory analysis used paired contingency counts (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00), paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729), and exact McNemar two‑sided test on discordant pairs. All raw responses, provider_call logs, scoring JSONs, seeds, and SHA256 digests are in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA256 31f4320f76703811a8d201ffc1530eedc8e11dfbdebdfe67c7ff162f24e6bbdb).
sections.results: Execution audit: planned episodes = 180; completed = 166; failed after preregistered retries = 14 (recorded in execution/execution_log.jsonl). Provider/model calls: hosted_model_call_event_count = 92; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7 (execution manifest). Paired analysis (complete pairs n=83): n_11 (both success) = 81; n_10 (guarded success only) = 2; n_01 (baseline success only) = 0; n_00 = 0. Derived metrics: baseline success = 81/83 = 0.9759036145; guarded success = 83/83 = 1.0000000000; absolute paired improvement = 0.0240963855. Paired bootstrap 95% CI (percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.50. Interpretation: the guarded judge changed two discordant pairs in these scripted emulator scenarios; the numerical effect is small and statistically inconclusive at the realized paired n.
sections.discussion: Analytic path and preregistration note: the preregistration specified a paired design and a primary estimand oriented to supported/unsupported classification (originally expressed as F1 on held‑out samples). Given the paired episode generation for each seeded task, the autonomous confirmatory analysis used within‑task paired contingency (McNemar) to exploit the counterfactual pairing (baseline vs guarded) and preserve within‑task inference; this analytic choice and its rationale are reported here and all scoring artifacts are preserved. Statistical interpretation: the paired bootstrap CI includes zero and McNemar p>0.05; with complete pairs n=83 the run is underpowered to detect very small absolute improvements—the observed CI upper bound (≈0.06024) quantifies the precision achieved. Provider‑call discrepancy and execution constraints: planned maximum_model_calls=180 vs model_calls_used=92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count=85, failed=7) reflect deterministic short‑circuiting, validator gating, and failed provider calls recorded in execution/provider_calls/*.json. The manifest documents these events and their SHA256 digests; they explain why several preregistered secondary/ablation analyses could not be completed within the realized call budget. Threats to validity: internal—prompt sensitivity, parser fragility, hosted LLM nondeterminism, and failed calls (all logged); construct—labels derive from deterministic emulator ground truth and omit production telemetry diversity; external—single model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic scenarios limit generality; conclusion validity—realized paired n reduces sensitivity to small effects. Reproducibility and artifacts: all raw responses, scoring JSONs, provider_call logs, execution logs, and per‑file SHA256 digests are enumerated in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA256 31f4320f76703811a8d201ffc1530eedc8e11dfbdebdfe67c7ff162f24e6bbdb). Sensitivity analyses planned in the preregistration (exclude flagged/replaced episodes; ablations of retrieval/validator/telemetry signals) were not fully executed because the realized provider call budget and failed calls prevented completion; these constraints are documented in the manifest. Operational implication: deterministic evidence gating is an auditable engineering control that may change a modest number of unsupported assertions in tightly controlled emulator settings; production deployment requires larger, multi‑model, telemetry‑rich evaluations and human‑in‑the‑loop thresholds to quantify cost/latency tradeoffs.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered, autonomous paired study of a deterministic provenance+validator judge vs an LLM baseline in scripted NetOps emulator scenarios. The guarded judge changed two discordant pairs among 83 paired tasks (absolute improvement 0.0240963855; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]; McNemar p = 0.50). The effect is numerically small and statistically inconclusive at the realized paired sample size. All execution artifacts (raw outputs, per‑call logs, scoring JSONs) and SHA256 digests are preserved in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA256 31f4320f76703811a8d201ffc1530eedc8e11dfbdebdfe67c7ff162f24e6bbdb). The conclusion is strictly bounded: deterministic programmatic evidence checks can affect a small number of unsupported LLM "no‑issue" assertions in controlled emulator conditions; broader claims about production utility or cross‑model generality are not supported by this run. Future work should run larger preregistered paired experiments, complete planned ablations, and evaluate human‑in‑the‑loop thresholds under production telemetry and latency/cost constraints.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed under the CNSM 2026 Agentic AI Researcher requirements with an autonomy lock and a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1). Human involvement before the autonomy lock: the Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps), approved the autonomy boundary, and approved the preregistration; all subsequent scientific actions after the autonomy lock were performed autonomously. LLM(s) and identifiers: the hosted model used in the confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Orchestration/framework: the frozen adapter family specified in the preregistration was hosted_netops_gvr_v1; the judge pipeline combined deterministic retrieval grounding (preregistered snapshot index), syntactic/semantic validators, and deterministic telemetry cross‑checks (all logic frozen in the preregistration). Exact initial master prompt: the immutable Master Prompt v1 that constrained autonomous behaviour was supplied in the frozen input bundle and is referenced by the preregistration; prompt templates and judge logic were frozen prior to execution (see execution/model_configuration.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Preregistration/freeze procedure: the preregistration fixed task bank size (90 seeded emulator scenarios), paired design, random seeds, retry/replacement rules (up to 2 retries), maximum_model_calls (180), stopping rules, primary/secondary estimands, and the analysis plan (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1). Autonomous procedures: literature review, experiment design selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, statistical testing, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review and revision were performed autonomously after the lock. Execution artifacts and provenance: all raw LLM responses, per‑call provider_call JSONs, parser outputs, scoring JSONs, seeds, and an execution manifest enumerating per‑file SHA256 digests were produced by the autonomous run and are the authoritative reproducible artifacts; representative artifact: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA256 31f4320f76703811a8d201ffc1530eedc8e11dfbdebdfe67c7ff162f24e6bbdb). Tools and capabilities permitted: the run used the hosted LLM provider API for gpt-5-mini and deterministic emulator scripts for NetOps scenarios; retrieval/index snapshot and local validator code were used as frozen components. Technical restarts and deviations: the execution followed the preregistered deterministic retry and replacement policy; 14 episodes failed after retries and were recorded; hosted_model_call_event_count = 92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7) as detailed in the execution manifest. Pre‑lock development: the Research Director and AI collaboratively developed and rehearsed infrastructure prior to the autonomy lock; per the CNSM rules, pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as evidence unless independently reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow. Autonomy boundary: humans set the topic family and approved the preregistration before lock; thereafter, the autonomous researcher selected the final research question, executed the study, analyzed results, drafted the manuscript, and performed revisions without manual human editing of technical content. No human manually edited or rewrote the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Limitations: experiments are limited to scripted synthetic/emulator scenarios and a single model (gpt-5-mini); several preregistered secondary/ablation analyses were not completed due to execution/model_call constraints; these limitations and all deviations are recorded in the execution manifest.
limitations: Evaluation limited to scripted synthetic/emulator scenarios; external validity to production NetOps environments is untested.
Single‑model experiment (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or versions.
Planned episodes (180) were not fully completed: 166 episodes completed, 14 failed after preregistered retries; complete paired tasks = 83, reducing confirmatory power for small effects.

Preregistered primary estimand was expressed as F1 on a held‑out split; the executed confirmatory analysis used a paired contingency / McNemar framework to leverage within‑task counterfactuals—this analytic choice is described and justified in the manuscript and affects inferential interpretation.

Several preregistered secondary metrics and ablations (precision/recall bootstrap CIs, calibration/Brier scores, retrieval/telemetry/validator ablations) were not fully executed to completion on the realized dataset and remain unresolved for this run.

Provider/model call budget discrepancy: planned maximum_model_calls = 180 vs model_calls_used = 92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85); the manifest records short‑circuiting and failed calls that explain the discrepancy but episode→call mapping is not strictly one‑to‑one.
Construct validity: supported/unsupported labels derive from deterministic emulator ground truth and may not capture production telemetry modalities or operator evidence practices.
